items.title: 'You always make me smile': Epstein files rock global monarchies
items.description: The latest release of the so-called Epstein files has revealed the convicted child sex offender was in contact with members of, and people close to monarchies across Europe and the Middle East.

items.title: Winds in excess of 200km/h forecast as Pilbara braces for Tropical Cyclone Mitchell
items.description: While avoiding a direct hit, Karratha is still expected to feel the force of the category three cyclone as it tracks along the Pilbara coast tonight.

items.title: 'Teflon president' may be no more as Trump does the unthinkable
items.description: Donald Trump has, until now, thrived in controversy. But the US president has now done something that a year ago would have been unthinkable: deleted a social media post.

items.title: Untying antisemitism from anti-Israel sentiment will take political courage
items.description: Unravelling the threads of antisemitism and anti-Israeli sentiment will require both more political courage and more community tolerance than we have seen to date.

items.title: Americans propose an end to Russian-Ukrainian war by June, Zelenskyy says
items.description: America has given Russia and Ukraine a June deadline to end the war — and will put pressure on both sides to ensure it is met — Volodymyr Zelenskyy says.

items.title: Live: Gu recovers from nightmare crash to qualify for slopestyle final
items.description: Two-time gold medallist Eileen Gu's Milano Cortina campaign gets off to the worst possible start as a former champion fails to qualify for the slopestyle final. Follow live.

items.title: Rabbi condemns derogatory slur spray-painted on Andrew Hastie's office
items.description: Police are investigating a derogatory slur spray-painted on federal MP Andrew Hastie's electorate office in Western Australia.

items.title: Trump described as 'sick individual' over video showing Obamas as apes
items.description: The video was part of a late-night posting spree centred on debunked conspiracy theories linked to the 2020 US election, which the president has falsely claimed was stolen from him.

items.title: NSW Police given extra powers ahead of Israeli presidential visit
items.description: NSW Premier Chris Minns has told demonstrators planning to protest Israel President Isaac Herzog's visit to Sydney that there should be "no clashes or violence".

items.title: 'Monster' funeral home owner sentenced over 189 counts of corpse abuse
items.description: A funeral home owner who stashed 189 decomposing bodies in a building over four years and gave grieving families fake ashes has been sentenced to 40 years in prison.

items.title: 'A screen shot of Mrs Doubtfire': Commemorative QEII coins mocked online as collectors snap them up
items.description: The portrait of Queen Elizabeth on two coins released by the Royal Australian Mint draws criticism, despite proving popular with collectors.

items.title: Prosecutors seek almost four-year sentence for US man linked to killers
items.description: US prosecutors are seeking a sentence of almost four years for a conspiracy theorist linked to the trio behind the Wieambilla shooting.

items.title: Daly River to hit major flood level Sunday, damage to homes expected
items.description: Almost 300 people from Daly River have been evacuated to Darwin, with just a handful of residents staying behind.

items.title: Family's warning after 27yo dies of suspected heatstroke on cattle station
items.description: Tiffani Phelps de Wildt died after collapsing on a remote station in WA's north. Her family says, had they known the risks, they would have tried to stop her from going out in the heat.

items.title: What our teeth reveal about the growing gap between rich and poor
items.description: Teeth are one of the most visible markers of poverty: structural circumstances that are individually borne.

items.title: A former ambassador has written a thriller about Europe's 'forgotten' war
items.description: Former ambassador Ian Kemish draws on his 25-year diplomatic career in his debut novel, Two Islands, set against the backdrop of the Balkan War.

items.title: 'I'm so lucky to get another crack': From an excavator to the NRL pre-season for this Wests Tigers hopeful
items.description: After three years away from first grade, Pat Herbert was ready to get on with the rest of his life but a call from Wests Tigers got him off the job site and into an NRL pre-season.

items.title: Australians chasing 'Japow' are running into problems on Japan's slopes
items.description: Australians flock to Japan each year to take advantage of its unique and plentiful snow, but it's not just the travel costs that are mounting.

items.title: Nancy Guthrie may have been abducted in a 41-minute window
items.description: Nancy Guthrie was last seen alive when a relative dropped her outside her Tucson home after a family games night. The 84-year-old grandmother has now been missing for a week.

items.title: A bigger economic story is unfolding beyond interest rates
items.description: As the opposition and government wrestled in the hay barn over who's to blame for this week's Reserve Bank interest rate increase, there's a much bigger story unfolding in the wings.

items.title: After US strikes, Iran accelerates work at secret underground nuclear site
items.description: Since the US bombed Iran's key nuclear sites last year, analysts say work has increased at a secret underground facility that could be used to restart Tehran's nuclear program.

items.title: The Mark of Cain lead singer on a lifetime masking the truth
items.description: The lead singer of legendary Adelaide rockers The Mark of Cain this week announced she was transgender, but it comes after nearly 60 years of hiding the truth from everyone.

items.title: 'They're afraid': Can Thailand's popular progressives finally win government?
items.description: As Thailand prepares to head to the polls, voters remain wary that in their version of democracy, the party they vote for is not always the one that takes power.

items.title: Queensland child safety minister denies knowledge of IT system failure
items.description: Queensland's child safety minister says she was not briefed about issues with a botched IT system that potentially put kids at risk.

items.title: Luigi Mangione speaks out against prospect of back-to-back trials
items.description: Accused killer has spoken out in court against the prospect of back-to-back trials over the shooting of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, telling a judge "it's the same trial twice".
